question.text: What sanctions can SEBI/the exchange impose on a trading member for non-compliance with ETIRD trading regulations?

answer.text: Monetary penalty, withdrawal of trading/clearing facilities, close-out of positions, collection of deposits, invocation of bank guarantees/FDRs, and other disciplinary action depending on severity
Only a verbal warning for first-time offenders
No penalties; SEBI can only issue advisory notices
Penalties apply only for criminal offenses, not regulatory violations

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series IV (pp.247, 263, 282), SEBI/exchanges can impose monetary penalties, withdraw trading/clearing facilities, close-out positions, collect/forfeit deposits, invoke bank guarantees or FDRs, and take other disciplinary action against intermediaries for settlement, margin, or other regulatory failures. The Trap: Enforcement goes well beyond verbal warnings or advisory notices, and applies to regulatory violations — not only criminal offences. Note: Specific sanctions like disgorgement or expulsion from membership exist under broader SEBI law but are not the sanctions enumerated on the checked source pages.
